partners.diseaseBName: vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, combined deficiency of, type 1
partners.mechanism_chain: Gamma-glutamyl carboxylase (HGNC:4247) —DISRUPTS→ Gamma-carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent proteins (GO:0006075); Gamma-carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent proteins (GO:0006075) —DECREASES→ Uncarboxylated vitamin K-dependent clotting factors (CHEBI:60881); Uncarboxylated vitamin K-dependent clotting factors (CHEBI:60881) —DISRUPTS→ Coagulation cascade (GO:0007596); Coagulation cascade (GO:0007596) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal hemostasis (HP:0001871); Gamma-glutamyl carboxylase (HGNC:4247) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital disorder of glycosylation (HP:0001368). Loss-of-function mutations in GGCX impair the gamma-carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent proteins, including clotting factors. This leads to the accumulation of uncarboxylated clotting factors, which are dysfunctional, disrupting the coagulation cascade and causing abnormal hemostasis (Disease B). Additionally, GGCX is involved in other post-translational modifications, and its dysfunction can lead to a broader spectrum of congenital disorders, including glycosylation defects which manifest as congenital disorder of glycosylation (Disease A).

partners.diseaseBName: thrombophilia, X-linked, due to factor 9 defect
partners.mechanism_chain: F9 (HGNC:3606) —DISRUPTS→ Activated Factor IX (CHEBI:58091); Activated Factor IX (CHEBI:58091) —LEADS_TO→ Coagulation Cascade (REACT:R-HSA-69904); Coagulation Cascade (REACT:R-HSA-69904) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding (HP:0001892); Coagulation Cascade (REACT:R-HSA-69904) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombophilia (HP:0001649). Loss-of-function mutations in F9 disrupt the production or activation of Factor IX, which is a critical component of the coagulation cascade. This impairment leads to a deficiency in clotting factors, manifesting as bleeding disorders (MONDO:0012570). Paradoxically, certain F9 mutations can also lead to thrombophilia (MONDO:0010432) through incompletely understood mechanisms, possibly involving dysregulation of anticoagulant pathways or altered thrombin generation.

raw.translational: Understanding the dual and opposing phenotypic outcomes (bleeding vs. thrombosis) arising from defects in the same gene (F9) and pathway (coagulation cascade) is crucial for developing targeted therapies. For bleeding disorders, replacement therapy with Factor IX is a standard treatment. For thrombophilia linked to F9, anticoagulation therapy is indicated. The challenge lies in differentiating these conditions and managing them appropriately.

partners.diseaseBName: thrombophilia due to protein C deficiency, autosomal recessive
partners.mechanism_chain: GGCX (HGNC:4369) —DISRUPTS→ vitamin K-dependent carboxylation (REACT:R-HSA-193047); vitamin K-dependent carboxylation (REACT:R-HSA-193047) —LEADS_TO→ GGCX-related disorders (MONDO:0012570); PROC (HGNC:9147) —DISRUPTS→ Protein C (UniProt:P04070); Protein C (UniProt:P04070) —DECREASES→ coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-69615); coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-69615) —LEADS_TO→ thrombophilia due to protein C deficiency, autosomal recessive (MONDO:0012860); vitamin K-dependent carboxylation (REACT:R-HSA-193047) —DECREASES→ coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-69615). Mutations in GGCX impair the vitamin K-dependent carboxylation pathway, leading to GGCX-related disorders. Concurrently, mutations in PROC lead to a deficiency in functional Protein C, which in turn dysregulates the coagulation cascade and results in thrombophilia. The shared convergence node is the coagulation cascade, as GGCX is involved in the proper function of multiple vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors, and Protein C is a key regulator of this same cascade.

partners.diseaseBName: thrombophilia due to protein S deficiency, autosomal recessive
partners.mechanism_chain: GGCX (HGNC:4345) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin K metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1987405); Vitamin K metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1987405) —DECREASES→ gamma-carboxylated clotting factors (CHEBI:60607); gamma-carboxylated clotting factors (CHEBI:60607) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal blood coagulation (HP:0001975); PROS1 (HGNC:9804) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin K metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1987405); Vitamin K metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1987405) —DECREASES→ Protein S (UniProtKB:P07225); Protein S (UniProtKB:P07225) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombophilia (HP:0011417). Loss-of-function mutations in GGCX (Disease A) and PROS1 (Disease B) converge on the shared pathway of Vitamin K metabolism, specifically impairing the gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors. GGCX is directly involved in this carboxylation process, while PROS1 encodes Protein S, a cofactor necessary for the activity of the vitamin K-dependent carboxylase. Defective carboxylation of general clotting factors leads to abnormal coagulation (Disease A), and deficient functional Protein S leads to thrombophilia (Disease B).

#### 1. vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, combined deficiency of, type 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.783)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:4247)

**Proposed mechanism:** Gamma-glutamyl carboxylase (HGNC:4247) —DISRUPTS→ Gamma-carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent proteins (GO:0006075); Gamma-carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent proteins (GO:0006075) —DECREASES→ Uncarboxylated vitamin K-dependent clotting factors (CHEBI:60881); Uncarboxylated vitamin K-dependent clotting factors (CHEBI:60881) —DISRUPTS→ Coagulation cascade (GO:0007596); Coagulation cascade (GO:0007596) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal hemostasis (HP:0001871); Gamma-glutamyl carboxylase (HGNC:4247) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital disorder of glycosylation (HP:0001368). Loss-of-function mutations in GGCX impair the gamma-carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent proteins, including clotting factors. This leads to the accumulation of uncarboxylated clotting factors, which are dysfunctional, disrupting the coagulation cascade and causing abnormal hemostasis (Disease B). Additionally, GGCX is involved in other post-translational modifications, and its dysfunction can lead to a broader spectrum of congenital disorders, including glycosylation defects which manifest as congenital disorder of glycosylation (Disease A).

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in GGCX that are associated with Disease A but not with Disease B, or vice versa, or identifying distinct causal genes for each disease. _(variant: rs74302622)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis highlights the potential for therapeutic strategies targeting the GGCX pathway or its downstream effects to benefit patients with either disorder. It also suggests that patients presenting with one disorder might be at risk for phenotypes associated with the other.
